name: Michael Jackson
hook: A Motown child star whose 1982 album is still the best-selling record ever made, and whose personal history includes two rounds of child sexual abuse allegations that remain part of how he is remembered.
blurb: Michael Jackson joined his brothers' group, the Jackson 5, as a Motown child star in the 1960s, then became a solo star. His 1982 album 'Thriller' sold roughly 70 million copies around the world and is still the best-selling album ever made. Its song 'Human Nature', written by Steve Porcaro and John Bettis and produced by Quincy Jones, is one of his most sampled recordings in hip-hop, including by Large Professor for Nas's 'It Ain't Hard to Tell' (1994). Jackson also faced serious allegations that he sexually abused children. A 1993 civil lawsuit was settled out of court in 1994 with no criminal charges filed, and at a criminal trial from 2003 to 2005 a jury found him not guilty on every count. After his death in 2009, the 2019 HBO documentary 'Leaving Neverland' presented accounts from two men, Wade Robson and James Safechuck, who said Jackson had abused them as boys. His estate has denied the claims and sued HBO over the film, a dispute that went on through the appeal courts. Both his huge musical influence and these allegations are part of the record here, stated without deciding how one should be weighed against the other.

signatureTracks.title: Human Nature
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: From 'Thriller'; its hook is the source for Nas's 'It Ain't Hard to Tell'.
